decisions.quote: Main: This claim was not replicated. The coefficient on the ‘diff’ (difference between IV and RV) is (positive) 0.07455682, but its p-value is 0.54497 (greater than 0.05).
decisions.reason: The central preregistered test ('Main') explicitly failed to replicate the original claim. The pre-Covid subsample analysis that succeeded was an unpreregistered robustness check and is excluded from the primary outcome under the central-finding rule.

parent_objection: The first reply invokes a central-finding rule to exclude an unregistered pre-Covid robustness check. The codebook does not generally exclude a tested original comparison merely because secondary or exploratory. Source labels Main: not replicated and Robustness Test: replicated, both testing the same original risk-premium claim on different sample periods. Is Main an overall verdict on the replication as a whole, or one of two original comparisons that require mixed under Rule 2? Read full report and exact codebook; distinguish this from new extensions to unrelated hypotheses. Do not invent an automatic preregistration-only rule. Explain source scope and retain unverified if genuinely ambiguous.
